body.heading: Separate the data from the drama
paragraphs: A wrong answer, a failed audition, a burnt first attempt: each contains a specific piece of information. The note was sharp. The timing was off. The pan was too hot. Specifics point somewhere useful.

What blocks the information is the drama layered on top — “I'm hopeless at this.” That sentence feels like a conclusion but contains no usable detail. Ask instead: what exactly happened, and what is one thing I could change?

body.heading: Keep a “learned” list
paragraphs: Some people keep a short list of things mistakes have taught them. It sounds odd, but watching that list grow reframes errors as tuition you have already paid — wasteful only if you refuse the lesson.
Not every mistake needs a deep analysis; some days you just fix it and move on. Save the reflection for the mistakes that repeat, because repeated ones usually guard the most useful information.

takeaway: Ask what the mistake is telling you, before you decide what it says about you.
